observation.visible_scene: Extreme close-up of a white, glossy painted form (skull-like) heavily splattered with cyan/blue paint, with a polished metal sphere embedded near its center and a thin dark filament arcing across the upper surface. A blurred orange/tan wall with dark spots fills the background. Numerous airborne particles—tiny blue specks, a small reddish-brown flake at left, and translucent blobs—hang in the foreground between camera and object.
visible_changes: The main white object, the embedded metal sphere, the dark filament, and the paint pattern stay fixed in the frame throughout the excerpt (no object translation or deformation is evident).
The small reddish-brown particle at left slowly translates leftward, moving from roughly x=175 at t=0 to x=110 at t=1.6.
The scattered tiny blue specks and the translucent foreground blobs drift gradually toward the left edge over the clip, consistent with suspended debris moving slowly.
The blurred background features (dark hole near top, vertical seam at left) hold constant positions, indicating the camera is stationary rather than panning.
The overall scene is quasi-static: the only visible motion is the slow lateral drift of the suspended particles against an unmoving object and background.
outside_clip_unknowns: What produced the suspended particles and the splattered paint (the triggering event is not in this crop).
Whether the particles were moving faster before t=0 or continue moving after t=1.6.
The true 3D depth and trajectory of each floating fragment.
uncertain_details: Whether the translucent shapes clinging to the object's left edge are attached broken material or free-floating debris passing in front.
Possible very subtle shifting of the blue translucent mass around the metal sphere, but no clear deformation is confirmed.
Exact direction of particle drift is inferred from a few trackable specks; most particles are too faint to follow reliably.

may already be underway in the first view and may continue beyond the last. The endpoints need
NOT match or connect as a loop. Do not judge different endpoints as a physical inconsistency,
and do not invent a trigger, contact, start, stop, landing, disappearance or completion to make
the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.
If an editing cut is visible inside the segment, distinguish it from continuous physical motion;
do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.
Describe what is visible during the excerpt, the actual changes, and supported persistent
properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;
do not invent causes, an earlier impact, an unseen operator, material identities or later outcomes.
Do not infer motion from one frame, a visible seam or a single pose. Static intervals are valid.
Do not supply named physics laws. Compare each important entity's first and last image positions
and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
Return JSON {"visible_scene":"...", "visible_changes":["observation supported within the excerpt"],
"outside_clip_unknowns":["unseen prerequisites or outcomes, only when relevant"],
